title: Good and wholesome
hook: eat of what is lawful and good (2:168), not just permitted but good

segments.voice: Yesterday: halal, the wide open middle, with a small fence around the forbidden. Your line was most things are allowed. Which of your five joys did you enjoy today? Day one hundred forty-four.

It's late. You're starving. There's a gas station, and inside it: a hot dog that has been rotating since the morning, a bag of neon chips, an energy drink the size of your forearm. Technically, most of it is allowed. Nothing on that shelf is on the short forbidden list, apart from the question of what's in the hot dog. But is it good? Allowed and good aren't the same question. The Qur'an, it turns out, names both. Today: good and wholesome.
screen: `A GAS STATION, LATE, STARVING.` → `TECHNICALLY ALLOWED.` → `BUT IS IT GOOD?`

segments.voice: Surah al-Baqarah, verse one hundred sixty-eight. In Pickthall's translation: O mankind! Eat of that which is lawful and wholesome in the earth. Two words, side by side. Lawful is halal, yesterday's word. Wholesome is today's: tayyib. Tayyib means good, pure, pleasant, clean, the kind of good you can taste and smell. The Qur'an uses it for food, but also for words: a good word, it says in Surah Ibrahim, is like a good tree, its roots firm and its branches in the sky. Notice the verse is addressed to all of mankind, not only to believers. And notice it asks for both. Halal is the line you don't cross. Tayyib is the direction you lean. A thing can be permitted and still not be good for you, or good for the people who made it, or good for the land it came from. Some Muslims today read tayyib that widely: food that is healthy, honestly earned, fairly made, humanely raised. Sahih Muslim has a hadith that shows why it matters. The Prophet ﷺ said: Allah is good, tayyib, and He accepts only what is good. Then he described a man on a long journey, hair wild, covered in dust, raising his hands to the sky and crying, O Lord, O Lord. The open hands were day one hundred thirty-one. But his food was unlawful, his drink unlawful, his clothes unlawful, and he was nourished on the unlawful. So how, the Prophet asked, could he be answered? In the hadith, what goes into a person reaches their prayer. Good in, good out.
screen: `2:168 — LAWFUL AND WHOLESOME.` · `TAYYIB — GOOD, PURE, PLEASANT.` · `HALAL IS THE LINE; TAYYIB, THE LEAN.` · `ALLAH IS GOOD, AND ACCEPTS THE GOOD.` · then, large: `GOOD IN, GOOD OUT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: eat one wholesome thing, slowly. If you have something nearby, a piece of fruit, a handful of nuts, a glass of water, take it now. If not, picture the last good thing you ate. Before the first bite, look at it. Where did it grow? Who picked it, packed it, carried it? If you pray, you can say bismillah. Then eat it slowly, one bite at a time, tasting it all the way through. Notice what good feels like, not just full. The bell holds the time.
Tayyib. Good, pure and wholesome: not just permitted, but good, for you and for everyone it touched on the way. Today's word.
Your line: lawful and good. At your next meal or purchase today, ask two questions instead of one: is it allowed, and is it good? Day one hundred forty-four.

howItsDone: Muslims look for food that is both halal, permitted, and tayyib, good and wholesome, and some today extend tayyib to health, honest earning and humane, fair production.

match.prompt: what's inside tayyib — tap the pairs.

myth: it begins 'O mankind!', speaking to everyone.
the Qur'an uses tayyib for words as well as food
a good word is like a good tree, roots firm, branches in the sky (Surah Ibrahim).
the verse asks for both: lawful, and good.

fork.setup: a traveler, dusty and disheveled, raises his hands and cries 'O Lord, O Lord'. but everything he eats, drinks and wears is unlawful. what does the Prophet ﷺ ask?
options: how could he not be answered?
why doesn't he pray in Arabic?
fork.reveal: Allah is good and accepts only what is good (Muslim 1015). what goes into a person goes into their prayer.

original.note: Arabic: good, pure, wholesome, paired with halal in 2:168.

trapdoor: what you thought: halal food just means no pork.
what it means: the Qur'an asks for food that is halal, allowed, and tayyib, good.
what a scholar hears: halalan tayyiban in 2:168, addressed to 'mankind'; 'Allah is tayyib and accepts only the tayyib' (Muslim 1015); 14:24.

sources.quoted: O mankind! Eat of that which is lawful and wholesome in the earth
